title: Nigerian Legal System II
topics: Access to justice and law reform
Historical foundations of the legal system
Sources and their order of precedence

items.q: Which term is described by “an enactment made directly by a body with power to make rules for the territory”?
o: Local enactment
Doctrine of equity
Hierarchy of sources
Principal legislation
items.s: Principal legislation is an enactment made directly by a body with power to make rules for the territory.
items.t: Sources and their order of precedence

items.q: Which of the following best describes Private prosecution?
o: the body chaired by the head of the judiciary that recommends candidates for the bench and disciplines errant ones
the conduct of criminal proceedings by a complainant without official backing
the authority given by the chief law officer permitting a private complainant to prosecute
the sworn undertaking to do right to all manner of people without fear or favour
items.s: Private prosecution: the conduct of criminal proceedings by a complainant without official backing. The other options describe Fiat, National Judicial Council, Judicial oath.

items.q: Call to the bar may be defined as
o: the practical ability of a person to bring a grievance before a tribunal, whatever his means
a remark on a point not necessary to the outcome, which does not bind
the formal admission of a graduate to practise after completing the vocational course
the process begun by a petition to the council and completed by an address of two thirds of the legislature
items.s: Call to the bar: the formal admission of a graduate to practise after completing the vocational course. The other options describe Removal of a judge, Access to justice, Obiter dictum.

items.q: The statement “the day fixed for measuring which English enactments entered the country, being 1 January 1900” describes which of the following?
o: Consular jurisdiction
Charter of 1861
Reception cut-off date
Warrant chief
items.s: Reception cut-off date is the day fixed for measuring which English enactments entered the country, being 1 January 1900.
items.t: Historical foundations of the legal system

items.q: Maliki school may be defined as
o: the highest rank at the bar, conferred on practitioners of distinction
the Sunni juristic tradition that governs personal questions in the northern states
the protection that a judge keeps office until a fixed retiring age and may be removed only by a special procedure
the authority exercised by British officials in the Niger Delta over disputes involving traders before annexation
items.s: Maliki school: the Sunni juristic tradition that governs personal questions in the northern states. The other options describe Consular jurisdiction, Security of tenure, Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Nolle prosequi?
o: the formal notice by the law officer that proceedings shall go no further
the colonial policy of governing through traditional authorities under the supervision of British officials
the setting aside of an earlier ruling by a tribunal higher in the hierarchy
the legal reason on which the outcome of a case rests
items.s: Nolle prosequi: the formal notice by the law officer that proceedings shall go no further. The other options describe Overruling, Indirect rule, Ratio decidendi.

items.q: The statement “a decision reached in ignorance of a binding rule or authority, which need not be followed” describes which of the following?
o: Ratio decidendi
Distinguishing
Per incuriam
Reversal
items.s: Per incuriam is a decision reached in ignorance of a binding rule or authority, which need not be followed.

items.q: Which term is described by “the voluntary body that speaks for practitioners and promotes professional standards”?
o: Contingency fee
Body of Benchers
Nigerian Bar Association
Fusion of the professions
items.s: Nigerian Bar Association is the voluntary body that speaks for practitioners and promotes professional standards.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Original jurisdiction.
o: the sufficient interest in a matter that entitles a person to sue
the power to hear a matter at first instance rather than on review
the rule that a practice fails where it conflicts with a written law in force
a traditional ruler given written authority by the colonial administration to exercise local judicial and administrative powers
items.s: Original jurisdiction: the power to hear a matter at first instance rather than on review. The other options describe Incompatibility test, Warrant chief, Locus standi.

items.q: All of the following belong to Islamic law in the north EXCEPT
o: Human rights commission
Alkali
Maliki school
Sharia
items.s: Every other option belongs to Islamic law in the north. “Human rights commission” belongs to Administration of justice, not Islamic law in the north.

items.q: Islamic personal rules may be defined as
o: the authority exercised by British officials in the Niger Delta over disputes involving traders before annexation
the Sunni juristic tradition that governs personal questions in the northern states
the authority given by the chief law officer permitting a private complainant to prosecute
the body of norms drawn from the Quran, the Sunnah and Maliki commentaries on marriage, succession and guardianship
items.s: Islamic personal rules: the body of norms drawn from the Quran, the Sunnah and Maliki commentaries on marriage, succession and guardianship. The other options describe Maliki school, Fiat, Consular jurisdiction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Valid custom.
o: a practice that is long established, reasonable, certain and consistent with natural justice
an action brought to protect a community concern rather than a private right
the agency that keeps persons committed to custody by the tribunals
the authority exercised by British officials in the Niger Delta over disputes involving traders before annexation
items.s: Valid custom: a practice that is long established, reasonable, certain and consistent with natural justice. The other options describe Public interest litigation, Consular jurisdiction, Correctional service.

items.q: Judicial decision may be defined as
o: the demonstration of a practice by evidence in the particular case
the voluntary body that speaks for practitioners and promotes professional standards
a remark on a point not necessary to the outcome, which does not bind
the reasoned ruling of a tribunal which may bind later tribunals on the same point
items.s: Judicial decision: the reasoned ruling of a tribunal which may bind later tribunals on the same point. The other options describe Obiter dictum, Proof of custom, Nigerian Bar Association.

items.q: Qualification for the bench may be defined as
o: the superior tribunal of a component unit with unlimited civil and criminal jurisdiction within its area
the setting aside of a decision of a lower tribunal by the one reviewing it in the same case
the years at the bar required before a practitioner may be appointed to a superior tribunal
the sufficient interest in a matter that entitles a person to sue
items.s: Qualification for the bench: the years at the bar required before a practitioner may be appointed to a superior tribunal. The other options describe Reversal, State High Court, Locus standi.

the protection that a judge keeps office until a fixed retiring age and may be removed only by a special procedure
the reasoned ruling of a tribunal which may bind later tribunals on the same point

the principle that a ruling of a higher tribunal must be followed by those below it on the same point
the position that only one named tribunal may hear a class of case
the settlement of a dispute by elders whose decision the sides bound themselves in advance to accept
